sources.title: Contextualizing Security and Privacy of Software-Defined Vehicles: A Literature Review and Industry Perspectives
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The study combines a systematic literature review with a targeted industry expert elicitation structured around four SDV security/privacy research questions.
The authors synthesize a security roadmap emphasizing mixed-criticality challenges, layered defenses, OTA/update risks, privacy controls, and coordination of in-vehicle and cloud-based protection.
The expert elicitation is explicitly exploratory and consensus-oriented rather than statistically generalizable.
claims.context: Methodological boundary stated by the authors.

metrics.name: expert questionnaire items
metrics.context: Questionnaire structure across definition, threats, mitigations, OTA and privacy sections.

limitations.text: The 11-response purposive expert sample is explicitly indicative rather than statistically generalizable.
Architecture/security statements summarize literature and practitioner judgment and should not substitute for normative standards or direct implementation evidence.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Contextualizing Security and Privacy of Software-Defined Vehicles: A Literature Review and Industry Perspectives; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The v4 full primary text verifies the systematic-review plus expert-elicitation methodology, 65-item questionnaire, 22-expert target list, 11 complete responses, and the authors' non-generalizability caveat.

editorial.why_now_note: Security, OTA and mixed-criticality concerns cut across every centralized/zonal layer and help bound what a viable SDV E/E architecture must protect.
editorial.rationale: High-quality context for cross-cutting security/privacy and mixed-criticality constraints, but it is a broad survey rather than a primary architecture mechanism; use mainly to frame risks and practitioner priorities.
